column2:
Great power in physical attack and defense: that is the
mark of the Warrior. If I must name a flaw... the slowest
movement of any class, narrow sight, and trouble both
using and resisting magic.

Even so, a Warrior's strengths more than make up for this.

In this lecture we shall study the Warrior and train to raise
its defining trait, Strength.

Quick to move, with sound defense against both physical
attacks and magic. Their physical attacks seldom miss,
and their sight is ample.

If I must name a flaw... they have no decisive strength.

Yet for that very reason they are versatile, and will prove
their worth in many situations.

In this lecture we shall study the Swordsman and train to
raise its defining trait, Agility.

Wide sight and the fastest movement of all. The long
reach of the bow makes physical attacks easy to use.

But defense is weak, against both physical attacks and
magic.

Find the enemy early and strike first from afar. Be the eyes
of Warriors and Mages, and take command of the field.
That is the Hunter's role.

In this lecture we shall study the Hunter and train to raise
its defining trait, Sense.

The Priest's greatest feature: attacks on the enemy
become healing for allies. Absolute defense against magic
is also a strength not to be overlooked.

But sight, movement, range and attack power are all
middling, and a Priest has no decisive blow of their own.

In this lecture we shall study the Priest and train to raise
what it rests upon, Virtue.

To wield a vast number of spells and pierce the foe from
astonishing range: that is what makes a Mage a Mage. The
power is overwhelming and, used well, can have
tremendous effect.

But against physical attacks they are all but naked, and
their sight is, to be polite, not wide. Much like the Warrior,
they are a mass of decisive blows with great flaws
besides.

In this lecture we shall study the Mage and train to raise
what it rests upon, Intelligence.

Start with small things. "Ah, it would feel so good if this
came about..." Just try doing a tiny bit of that.

My own master once taught me:
"Ask not after your own gain.
Only never forget the gain of others."
Even now I believe... that this will surely be the heart that
holds up the Shield of Purity.

Throughout history, in every land, magic has been created
in vast variety, and is still studied as eagerly as ever. To
call it all simply "magic" is far too crude, and it was long
ago that it was sorted into several fields.

The Shield of Purity mainly teaches by element, since
sorting by nature is the most intuitive.

Now, here we shall take the old magic that is the
foundation of all else. With elementless Void spells at the
center, let us study magic at our leisure.

Wind is the very symbol of freedom, bound by nothing.
Among spells it is the element whose power arrives
fastest, and its benefit to a caster is beyond measure. In
sheer force, though, it generally gives way to most others.

Why, then, do I love to chant the magic of wind? Because
it is bound by no situation, and readily gives the steady
power a caster wants. Swiftness! That is prized at all
times.

Here I shall teach with the weight on wind magic.

Magic changes its form with its element. And it is only
natural that the caster's own strength has great influence
here. Knowledge and strength of mind are not all that
shape a spell.

From here on... look widely across the foothills. I look
forward to you becoming sages fit to command great
magic.

I am Denehere Ruverdracloa. Some call me the Head of
Wings, but I am little different from a drifter.

At about your age, I met a certain mage. Captivated by
those superb spells, I tried every trick I knew to become
that mage's pupil.

What you love, you do well. If my wind magic can help you
find what it is you love, I shall be glad.

Hm? You still wish to hear this old bag of bones? Then
that, for both of us, is where the lecture begins.

The point of a lecture is to gain what quests cannot give.

It is essential above all for discovering the many skills. By
attending lectures in the field you wish to know, and in
related ones, you will awaken to skills along with ability.

Studying your specialty soundly, with no detours: that is
the strength of a lecture. Let us begin with some idle talk
here, and I hope to convey something of the charm of
sitting at a desk and devoting your passion to something.

The mark of a quest is, above all, the great experience
gained in real battle. Finding buried treasure is also well
worth mentioning. And sometimes a skill comes to you
along the way.

However, it is hard to aim for a skill you want through
quests alone. That much you should know.

It is presumptuous to teach anyone, but I can at least
teach the joy of drawing.

Never mind complaints. First, try drawing for yourself.
See, learn, touch, draw, and look again. That building and
turning over brings life to many other things.

I am Faldra Belis. I have mostly studied as a Priest, but
much travel has toughened my body. In a long life there
were times I had to take up a sword as well.

And strangely, I came to see things I could not as a Priest. I
have been scorned as a jack of all trades, yet there are
places where just such a one shines. Mind you, how you
wish to live is up to you.

Clerical arts are my greatest strength. If you have the
heart to attend to my words, you may suddenly awaken to
a skill.

Still, each of us has strengths and weaknesses. Never sulk
if you fail to find what you seek at the first try. Patience, I
hold, is the most important thing in learning magic.

And what of you, I wonder?

Clerical arts have two faces, light and dark. Though they
cannot coexist, the two are inseparable.

This has in truth caused much misunderstanding. To
those who do not know, darkness suggests not peace but
fear and evil.

It may be good experience to take on so ill-used a field,
don't you think?

I, Papesh Fake, meant only to drop in for a moment, but it
was so comfy I ended up staying... so I'd better repay the
bed and board.

Village, town or country, wherever there are good
Hunters, fine pride takes root. A Swordsman never brings
down a deer, and even a great Mage is badly matched for
setting spirits on one.

So if you're going to listen to me... be confident, and really
hone your skills.

In battle or on the hunt, what counts is focus. And above
all a feel for balance, a sense of "about like this." Say so
and they'll call you sloppy and careless, and that's exactly
right. I have no use for too much muscle, or too much
wisdom and virtue.

Put that clutter down, and take up a block of wood and a
chisel instead. If you can carve until you forget your
hunger, there's no gap for your arrow to land but the
enemy's weak spot.

You want to hear about bows? Well, there are all kinds...
but with a good bow, even the sound of the string is a
pleasure. Of course, if the player's no good, that lovely
melody's wasted.

If you'd like to play a chord that soothes the front line
even a little, today might be a good chance, don't you
think?

Just as light has its paired dark, Hunters too have a front
and a back. If looking straight ahead and playing fair is the
front world, then taking a slanted stance and laying traps
like a schemer would be the back.

The Hunter's back arts have a strange feel to them... so if
you plan to go on living decently, maybe don't get too
close, okay?

I'd rather not have taught this one. I mean, a Hunter using
a sword... That's just not supposed to happen.

But life is long. Once or twice you'll hit that kind of mess.
And the day will surely come when you can't say, for
anything, "I can only go to battle with a bow."

Then all that's left is to grip a sword. A Hunter welcomes
being light on their feet, and what you learn as a Hunter
really helps a Swordsman too.

Mind you, even if you aren't a Hunter... I won't slack off, so
don't worry.

If you want to master the Hunter, then of course I
recommend taking this.

But for a Hunter, a sense of balance is your lifeline. Don't
get so fixed on mastery that you lose something
important.

Got that? When you lose it, it really is gone in the blink of
an eye.

I am Cheryl Genowarth.

Until I can return to St. Sevies... I will serve the Shield of
Purity as an aide.

I am still far short of Lady Navilos and Lord Fald. But for as
long as I am here with you all, I will do my very best.

I look forward to working with you.

The words of light that Priests hold high have long been
equated with words of healing. So one may not claim to
be a Priest without the power to heal.

I too am still learning. Let us work hard together.

...The stillness that pairs with light and upholds motion. I
wish to teach you the darkness that governs peace.

Because it has been misunderstood and charged with
crimes it never did, I will not run or hide. Even a single
fragment of truth is enough. I hope you will sense the
shape of darkness, its thoughts, along with its secret arts.

To serve for the class, and for Elmenas: that is the aim of
this lecture. Notably, all the experience gained here is
stored up in the class, to use as you like.

Please learn all you can.

The Rite of Silence is at once the most elementary and
most important lecture at St. Sevies. I believe it can do
much good in the Shield of Purity too.

Lowering your eyes, closing your lips... Is that the same as
fleeing from reality? No. To listen for the voice within and
find the flame lit deep in your breast is to turn your eyes
to a garden you never even tilled. The rules carved into
your heart... have you forgotten even to tend them? Too
close to see?

Three things to say first. They apply always, and to
everyone, at least as far as the eye of this Batra Fedrinsk
can see.

One, greet people heartily, with their feelings in mind.
One, answer clearly, from the heart.
One, right your errors with all your strength, and fear not
to apologize.

What all can do, let all do together, shall we?

Have wisdom rather than knowledge. Weighty words,
yet knowledge does no harm. If wisdom is the power to
use tools well, then knowledge is the tools themselves.

As tools are neither good nor evil, so knowledge too is
pure and innocent.

Either way, you are the ones who use it. At the least, do
not forget to polish your tools.

No study is as motley as magic. Here, shall we confine
ourselves to water?

What matters in water magic is suppleness. That spirit,
clinging to no shape, is worthy to be called a teacher not
only by Mages but by anyone.

Though Papesh would say that all the world is a teacher.

Well, few things go well from the start. Accept that you will
fail, and give it a try.

In magic, the element of earth is mostly suited to defense.
On a long road of battles it is sure to prove valuable.

Earth is, by the by, the opposite of the wind magic the
Head of Wings favors, so the Shield of Purity has rarely
touched on it until now, hasn't it?

One or two earth users would surely bring great benefit to
the Shield of Purity.

Gerait Robery. My title's Priest, but... well, I've certainly
worn a lot of hats.

As Priest, Teacher Cheryl has seniority, so I'd like to spend
my share on the use of the greatsword. Sure, I've been
called an unreliable Warrior, but I don't plan on losing to
chicks like you just yet.

In other times there'd be plenty more fit for this... but at
the Academy as it is now, well. Innocentia made quite a
find, if you ask me.

Honestly, I don't think this is a thing teaching can do
much about. It's far too big a study to wrap up in fancy
words.

But... some will lean forward, eyes shining, at a bard's
legends and tales. They'll give you a straight look.

Don't you want to see it? The scene reflected in those
eyes.

What matters in chanting holy verses is not knowing their
meaning or pronunciation, nor boosting their effect, nor
competing in splendor.

Just one thing: keep in step with everyone as you chant.
To do that, you need to know the meaning and
pronunciation. Listen, don't mix up the goal and the
means.

Get that right, and you'll start to see what clerical arts are
all about.

A shortage of people really is a pain. I did agree to this
once, but I never thought the day would come when I'd
actually be instructing anyone on Warriors.

...Honestly, I don't dislike the sword. If anything, I like it.
But sadly, the more you like a thing, the more pitiful it can
get.

Still, well, you know. Compared with anyone learning the
sword from the Head of Keys... you lot might have some
hope.

Bright, lively, cheerful... a fine class.

I hear some of you joined only recently. I too intend to
tackle this with fresh spirit. By the flame of Baubes
Foretod... I shall do my best.

Now, let us bow to one another and begin.

So you desire flame? Yet without solid firewood, a flame
cannot grow.

If your resolve is unshaken, first build a firm foundation in
this lecture. Then I promise to teach you the supreme
flame.

The season is good. The time when blazing flame is spun
from your words of power cannot be far off.

Seek it, I beg you, with all your spirit.
It has been long since I last visited Innocentia. I, Navilos\nLucifuge, governing dark and light, hereby vow to lend\nyou all the aid I can.

Cut off the light, cut off the sound... Soon a deafening
noise will ring out, and little by little you will sink into
yourself.

Joys, hates, passing things, things you wished to forget...
And in time, will you realize? That endless feeling asleep
deep in your heart supports you and watches over you.

"Silence is not to be cut off from the world.
Contemplation is to unearth all, seen and unseen, that
holds you up, and to think on it with deep thanks.
And so, when you break your silence, you are borne up by
surging passion."

I shall teach you clerical arts. They will surely serve you on
your journey.

I need say no more. Follow, on your own two feet.

...In lectures, I am your teacher. And yet, I, Schneidra
Balesti, came to the Shield of Purity intending to learn
anew.

The smallest thing will do. Tell me. Please teach me, even
the merest fragment of what you have learned here.

All I can do is teach magic. And there is nothing in it but
reason.

Looking back, it was a barren road I came by. Heh... I
trampled everything underfoot. It is only what I deserve.

But for that very reason, I wish to teach you here. By
laying the heart of the Shield of Purity over my magic... I
hope to find a new road. I look forward to working with
you.

Crossing ridges, conquering peaks. Plodding along
borders like that is a sage's duty. Even where names are
unknown and no one speaks your tongue, sound legs will
usually get you there.

I won't say don't make a face... but do try hard.

"The view that opens from a ridge walk sets a great gap
between you and those who have not walked it."

This saying, by an unknown author, has lasted because it
speaks the truth. A lecture worth taking at least once.

A deep forest. The shore of a little pond. The window of a
ruined temple.

I want you to gaze... without lighting any rude lamp, on
you and all that surrounds you.

Sages really do go all kinds of places. Mountains, rivers,
plains, highlands, marshes, forests... with fun and danger
side by side. Rain, wind, bugs, snakes, wolves, cold, heat...

How do you choose a restful spot? Is water near or far?
Can you light a fire? Make the best meal you can,
efficiently, then sleep soundly. If you can do that...

It's your own lives at stake, so learn it well.

For getting food and water, for talking with the trees and
meeting spirits... the forest will be your greatest ally.

But if you fail to keep what must be kept, the rich forest
soon becomes a den of fearsome wildness.

Usually you'll fail once or twice, sometimes again and
again. In doing so, you become a true traveler.

Here, I'll teach you a few ways to make friends with the
journey.

At sea or on a lake, how you set your sail comes down to
how you read the wind. You'll get nowhere glued to a
desk.

Sometimes you must row out and feel it on your skin. Of
course, you can't do that in battle. And that one point is
just what makes a lecture worthwhile.

Take the wind and spray full on, and work sail and oar
with your own arms. If you can handle a boat the same in
calm and in storm, you've made it.

Well, few like that exist... apart from the head of the Shield
of Purity.
